title: POC hosting decision checkpoint - Northstar Manufacturing
header:
Date: 2027-08-16
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Sophie Lin (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Northstar CTO), Priya Menon (Head of ML), James Park (Infra Lead), Ana Gomez (Security)
Recording: yes (auto-transcript)
Notes: follow-up to initial discovery; focus on deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), workload sizing, success criteria, and benchmark plan.
summary: Checkpoint call to align POC success criteria and pick deployment path. Northstar is evaluating Hosted for speed-to-market, Dedicated for predictable latency, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency and audit requirements. Key constraints: P95 latency target, encryption/KMS, SOC2 audit needs, and 6-week pilot timeline. Agreed to run two benchmark sweeps (latency and cost) and produce a short test harness. Next: Redwood to deliver benchmark plan and pricing delta; Northstar to provide sample workload traces and SSO/KMS contact details.
topics: Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
action_items: Maya Patel; Send benchmark plan + spreadsheet with test matrices; 2027-08-18
Priya Menon; Share 2 weeks of inference traces (sampled) and typical prompt mix; 2027-08-19
Carlos Nguyen; Prepare quick perf-run runbook for Dedicated and Hosted (what we'll measure); 2027-08-20
Ana Gomez; Share SOC2 report and KMS vendor details required for Private deployment review; 2027-08-23
James Park; Provision short-lived VPC test endpoints for throughput runs (if Private path chosen); 2027-08-25
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark plan and model/config recommendations
Northstar to upload workload traces and security constraints doc
Schedule 2-hour benchmarking window week of Aug 24th
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and pick deployment mode: target Aug 27th
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 70 minutes so we can get through plan and alignment.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Yep thanks, Maya. Priya and James and Ana are with me. We want to make sure we pick the right deployment.
[00:20] Priya Menon: Quick context — our ML model is a retrieval augmented generation pipeline, mostly 2048 token contexts, average response ~320 tokens. Peak QPS around 15 for first phase, target 50 in phase two.
[00:35] Carlos Nguyen: Got it. That matters for batching and KV cache behavior. If you're using long context, that changes memory footprint and kernel selection.
[00:45] James Park: Our infra constraint — we need predictable latencies for operator dashboards, P95 ideally under 350ms. Cost is also a factor, but SLAs come first.
[00:58] Maya Patel: Understood. So tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest onboarding and we can start the POC in days. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and stable latency; Private gives you full control for KMS/audit but longer setup.
[01:15] Ana Gomez: For us security is non-negotiable: we need KMS integration, SSO, audit logs, and SOC2 + ISO references. Private would be easiest but we want to understand what Hosted/Dedicated can do for encryption in transit and at rest.
[01:30] Sophie Lin: We support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has envelope encryption and we can arrange bring-your-own-key for enterprise tiers — I'll attach the doc.
[01:44] Priya Menon: On accuracy/regression: we need a baseline eval set. We'll accept a small hit if latency drops, but not more than 2% drop in F1/metric.
[01:58] Maya Patel: Good — so POC success criteria draft: 1) P95 latency <= 350ms for tail LLM calls in dedicated setup, 2) token cost under $X per 1k tokens (we'll quantify), 3) no more than 2% quality regression on eval set, 4) integration with KMS/SSO or clear path, and 5) operational runbook for failover.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: That seems fair. Timeline? We need a go/no-go in six weeks.
[02:29] Carlos Nguyen: Plan proposal: week 0–1: exchange traces and access; week 2: Redwood runs hosted latency sweep and provides numbers; week 3: set up Dedicated reserved nodes and run comparable sweeps; week 4: optional Private exploratory run if required; week 5: analyze results; week 6: decision and pilot cutover.
[02:50] Priya Menon: For the benchmarks, what specifically will you measure?
[02:55] Carlos Nguyen: We'll measure cold and warm latencies, KV cache hit impact, sustained throughput, and token burn/cost. Also degradation under concurrency (spike tests). We'll provide scripts to replay traces.
[03:10] James Park: Replay scripts — we need language about synthetic vs replayed traces. Live traffic won't be shared; we'll give sampled traces.
[03:18] Maya Patel: That's fine. Replayed traces + sampled real traces are sufficient. We'll correlate sequence lengths and prompt mixes.
[03:26] Ana Gomez: A couple security Qs: are audit logs available at token-level? Can we redact PII in logs?
[03:33] Sophie Lin: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has retention controls and we can set up log forwarding on enterprise. Redaction is done client-side — we can add filtering hooks.
[03:47] Liam O'Connor: What about failover — if a region dies do you have automatic fallback to another region or lower-tier model?
[03:54] Carlos Nguyen: Yes we support smart routing: you can configure regional fallbacks and model variant fallbacks. During POC we'll test fallback latency penalty.
[04:05] Priya Menon: About Dedicated — how long to provision GPUs and what sizes?
[04:12] Maya Patel: Typically 3–5 business days to reserve; depending on GPU type (A10G-ish or A100) and your commit. For the POC we usually provision smaller pool with burst options.
[04:24] James Park: Cost modelling — can you provide delta between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private on token cost and infra amortized?
[04:30] Maya Patel: We'll provide a spreadsheet with amortized cost per 1k tokens for each path and assumptions on batching and KV cache hit rate. Carlos will propose quantized models to reduce per-token cost.
[04:43] Carlos Nguyen: Note: quantization can cut memory and cost but may affect output quality. We'll run a quantization check against your eval set — that becomes part of the quality criteria.
[04:55] Ana Gomez: Any compliance gotchas for Private on-prem? We have air-gapped segments and HSMs for KMS.
[05:02] Sophie Lin: Private supports on-prem installs and HSM integrations; lead time is longer and we may need a short security review cycle. We'll include compliance engagement in the plan.
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: Ok, benchmark specifics — can you outline the two sweeps you mentioned?
[05:21] Carlos Nguyen: Sweep A: Hosted baseline — run sampled traces with 3 concurrency levels (low, med, high) and measure cold/warm P95 and throughput. Sweep B: Dedicated reserved nodes with identical trace replay and spike bursts to measure stability and tail latencies. Optional Sweep C: Private VPC run to validate KMS flow and residency if required.
[05:44] Priya Menon: How do you simulate cold vs warm?
[05:47] Carlos Nguyen: Cold = after a short idle period without warmed KV cache; warm = concurrent runs with KV cache hits simulated based on your trace. We'll also instrument KV hit ratio in results.
[05:58] Maya Patel: For acceptance, we'll look at P95, 99th, median, CPU/GPU utilization, and qualitative checks against eval set.
[06:08] James Park: On the topic of ops — what observability will we get? Token-level cost, per-route latency, traces?
[06:14] Sophie Lin: Redwood Console gives per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, trace IDs, and SLO alerting. We'll include a preview and screenshots.
[06:27] Priya Menon: Are there any rate limits in Hosted that'll affect our test?
[06:31] Maya Patel: Hosted has limits on free tiers but enterprise tiers and POC accounts can be configured to match your target QPS for tests. We'll request an elevated quota window for the benchmark runs.
[06:44] Liam O'Connor: If Dedicated meets latency but cost is higher, is there a hybrid — e.g., Hosted for non-critical routes and Dedicated for low-latency ones?
[06:52] Carlos Nguyen: Yes hybrid routing is a common pattern. You can do smart routing by route or by token budget. We'll show examples in the plan.
[07:05] Ana Gomez: Data residency for EU customers — do you have region restrictions? Our EU line of business requires EU-only hosting.
[07:12] Sophie Lin: We have region controls and you can pin workloads to region. Private gives the strongest guarantee. Hosted can be pinned to regional data centers but we need to confirm cross-region backups.
[07:25] Priya Menon: About metrics — can you capture quality drift over time during the POC?
[07:30] Carlos Nguyen: We'll wire a small eval harness that runs a test prompt set periodically and logs diffs. Redwood Optimize can trigger alerts if regression crosses threshold.
[07:42] Maya Patel: Let's talk deliverables: Redwood will send benchmark plan + spreadsheet, quickstart scripts for trace replay, and model/config suggestions. Northstar to send traces + compliance doc.
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Who owns KMS integration in Dedicated? Our infra or Redwood?
[08:00] Sophie Lin: It's a joint effort: we provide the integration guide and Redwood engineers work with your security team. For Private we can do onsite or remote integration support.
[08:12] Priya Menon: Small nit — will quantized models be supported in Hosted? Sometimes we need int8 for costs.
[08:18] Carlos Nguyen: Hosted supports quantized variants for verified models; we'll show which models have int8/int4 paths. Some open models are more quant-friendly.
[08:28] James Park: If we run into a throughput bottleneck, is autoscaling immediate?
[08:33] Maya Patel: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies but there's a lead time to add GPUs; for burst capacity we offer pre-warmed burst pools for POCs.
[08:44] Ana Gomez: Any paperwork for elevated quotas or Dedicated provisioning?
[08:48] Maya Patel: We'll send a short SOW for the POC and a proposed commitment for Dedicated trial resources.
[08:57] Priya Menon: Ok let's call out explicit success criteria here so it's written down.
[09:02] Maya Patel: I'll read back the POC success criteria — please interrupt if wrong: 1) Performance: P95 latency <= 350ms on Dedicated baseline for typical prompt mix; 2) Quality: <= 2% degradation on your eval set; 3) Security: KMS or equivalent integration validated; 4) Observability: token-level cost and per-route traces available; 5) Timeline: go/no-go decision within 6 weeks.
[09:27] Priya Menon: That mirrors our internal ask, yes.
[09:30] Liam O'Connor: If Dedicated passes perf but Hosted is close enough with lower cost, can we consider hybrid?
[09:36] Carlos Nguyen: Yes and we'll quantify cost/latency delta in the spreadsheet.
[09:41] Sophie Lin: For the benchmark window week of Aug 24th — can we lock 2–3 days for the runs?
[09:46] James Park: We can support Aug 25–26 for runs and will provision test endpoints.
[09:50] Maya Patel: Great, we'll send invite and artifacts.
[10:00] Priya Menon: Quick question about model versions — can we pin model versions across environments so tests are apples-to-apples?
[10:07] Carlos Nguyen: Yes you can pin model versions and we recommend doing that for the POC. We'll provide a compatibility matrix for hosted/dedicated/private variants.
[10:18] Ana Gomez: Regarding audit logs and retention — we need 90-day retention in immutable logs for compliance.
[10:25] Sophie Lin: We can configure retention and forward to your immutable store for Dedicated/Private; Hosted might need an enterprise add-on. We'll include details.
[10:35] Liam O'Connor: Ok that answers most concerns. Any other blockers?
[10:39] Priya Menon: Nothing from ML side — just need the trace format examples.
[10:43] James Park: Infra: share estimate of network egress and any firewall rules you need.
[10:48] Maya Patel: We'll include a short network prep doc with required ports and egress estimates.
[10:55] Carlos Nguyen: I'll also include guidance on expected GPU memory per model at 2048 context so you can size nodes.
[11:05] Maya Patel: Sounds like we're aligned. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[11:12] Liam O'Connor: Thank you everyone.
[11:15] [call ends]
notes: Benchmarks will include cold/warm P95 and KV cache impact. Emphasis on SSO/KMS for Dedicated/Private. Plan to run tests Aug 25-26. Decision target Aug 27. Pricing spreadsheet to follow.
final_recap: Redwood to send: benchmark plan + pricing delta; Northstar to send traces + security constraints. Schedule tests Aug 25-26. Follow-up review Aug 27 for deployment decision. Agreed success criteria: P95 <= 350ms, <=2% quality drop, KMS integration validated, token cost model provided.
